clue.text: Jog up and I will start to arrange food

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to go for a run and then sort out the cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: TROT written upwards becomes TORT; the apostrophe of I'LL is ignored, as punctuation always is in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a flat Mexican bread, or a Spanish potato omelette, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Disregard unsettled region

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed from its resting state, so its letters move around

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to a troubled part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettled' reads as describing a restless region, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to pay no attention to something or someone, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Arrived with artist to get photographic equipment

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A photographer turns up with a painter to collect their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply puts the two pieces side by side; RA (Royal Academician) is the stock crossword abbreviation for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device used to take photographs, so it is the central item of photographic kit.

clue.text: Doctor hurt ref to a greater degree

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or falsify it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A medic treats an injured referee, or an injured referee is hurt even more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medic tending the injured official, but here it is a verb meaning to tamper with the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, further means more or additionally, to a more advanced extent.

clue.text: Hot tune and dance – something coming out of Cats?

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A lively song and dance number from the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Cats suggests the Lloyd Webber musical, full of tunes and dances; the question mark signals the literal animals instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats swallow fur while grooming and cough up the compacted wad, so a hairball literally comes out of them.

clue.text: Conclude Flipper is inhaling a line and another drug

indicators.note: breathing in draws air inside the body, so one piece is taken into the middle of the other

blocks.note: a fin or flipper is a swimming limb
L is the abbreviation for line
E is ecstasy; 'another' because a line is also slang for a dose of cocaine

explanation.surface: Flipper the dolphin is caught snorting a line of cocaine and taking another drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipper is' must be read as two pieces that together swallow the 'a line' pair. Flipper is the dolphin of a famous 1960s TV series, and E (ecstasy) is the stock crossword drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To finalise something is to complete it or settle it, which is to bring it to a conclusion.

clue.text: Pass on knowledge to popular student group

blocks.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A teacher shares what they know with a well-liked class.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone is to tell them facts, giving them information they lacked.

clue.text: Cook left a cut roasting on for well done

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: leave a joint of meat roasting if you want it well done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' looks like the cooking degree for meat, matching 'roasting', but it is the exclamation of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are expressions of praise offered to someone on an achievement or success.

clue.text: Tried to wander next to street

indicators.note: being beside something means the two pieces simply sit side by side in a row

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone attempted a stroll along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next to' places the wandering word beside the street abbreviation, which comes first here.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning made a great effort, so it equals tried.

clue.text: Herb is strangely arrogant

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A man called Herb is oddly conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' reads as a man's name, but it is the plant being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic culinary plant used in French cooking, an example of a herb.

clue.text: Cut off a story by Nathaniel

blocks.note: a story can be a fib

explanation.surface: An abridged tale written by Nathaniel Hawthorne, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' looks like a description of a shortened story, but it is the definition; 'story' means a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to isolate or estrange them, making them feel separated from others.

clue.text: Pivotal line about yogic sacred syllable principles

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: an axis is the line something turns on
om is the syllable chanted in meditation

explanation.surface: A key teaching in yoga concerning the sacred chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pivotal' looks like 'crucial', but here it means turning on a pivot; the axis is split around OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Axioms are self-evident truths or rules taken as the basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Beat young animal with a stone

blocks.note: a lamb is a young sheep
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a lamb with a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to thrash someone physically, or to attack them harshly in words.

clue.text: Remade blouses to include core of rayon as response to sign of cold

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so only the middle letter is kept
including something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside
something remade is put together afresh, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Blouses are remade with rayon at their heart to keep someone warm in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y goes into BLOUSES and the whole lot is rearranged; 'sign of cold' is a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what people traditionally say when someone sneezes, and sneezing is a symptom of a head cold.

clue.text: Upset about LA pub food offering

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy about the menu at a Los Angeles pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' wants to be an anagram signal for the following letters, but here it is an adjective meaning unhappy, and 'about' does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad bar is a counter where customers serve themselves salads, a self-service food provision.

clue.text: Both sides of appeal studied by Yankee beforehand

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters stay

blocks.note: the first and last letters of appeal
to read a subject is to study it
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American looked over both sides of a legal appeal in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: At British universities one 'reads' a subject, so studied gives READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means before now or before the time in question, which is the same as previously.

clue.text: Ruin his model arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a man's carefully set out model display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' sits at the end as a noun, signalling that the preceding letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish is to wreck or destroy completely, so it can mean to ruin.

clue.text: One playing with a carbon lock

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone fiddling with a carbon-steel lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door fastening, but it is a lock of hair; 'playing' is acting a part.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress plays roles on stage or screen, so she is a performer who plays parts.

clue.text: Sailor leans back in descent with rope

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word runs right to left

blocks.note: to lie against something is to lean on it

explanation.surface: A sailor reclines while being lowered on a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: AB (able-bodied seaman) is the standard crossword sailor; 'leans back' looks like a posture, but 'back' turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: An abseil is a controlled slide down a rock face or building on a rope fixed above.

clue.text: Island carried nothing

blocks.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: An island that had no cargo at all.
explanation.walkthrough: BORNE is the 'carried' form of bear, distinct from BORN for birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is the large island in South-East Asia shared by Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

clue.text: Appeal from cleaner is oddly mean

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and so on are kept

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
first and third letters of mean

explanation.surface: A cleaner's charm hides a stingy streak.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm or attractiveness that draws others in.

clue.text: After middle of day release relative

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A family member is let out of custody in the early afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the releasing word follows the central letter; 'middle of day' looks like noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is an informal name for an aunt, a parent's sister and so a family member.

clue.text: One with new shelter finding purpose

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A homeless person given fresh housing discovers a reason to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An intent is an aim or intention, the thing someone means to achieve.

clue.text: Campaigner is unusually scared about game

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters come in an uncommon order
about means around, so one piece goes around the other

explanation.surface: An activist is uncharacteristically nervous about a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap around RU after their first letter; RU (rugby union) is a common crossword game.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who fights vigorously for a cause, a zealous campaigner for change.

clue.text: Annoy weed

blocks.note: second meaning: a stinging wild plant

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it is an instruction to pester a weed; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to irritate or provoke, and the noun is a stinging plant common in gardens.

clue.text: Hates John’s views about person calling round uninvited?

indicators.note: about can mean all around or in disorder, so the letters are scattered and reset

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone loathes John's opinions on unexpected visitors at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it is the anagram signal for the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Christian denomination are known for evangelising door to door without appointment, hence the question mark.
